thesis.what_must_be_true: The AI infrastructure build-out must keep leading-edge logic (GAA at 2nm), DRAM/HBM and advanced packaging capex compounding through CY2027; Applied must convert its deliberately enlarged build plan and inventory into shipments at ≥50% non-GAAP gross margin; China must fade as a share of revenue without shrinking the total; and capital returns (~$8–9B/yr buybacks plus a growing dividend) must continue shrinking the share count so mid-teens revenue growth becomes high-teens EPS growth. If WFE spending stalls or export rules remove another slice of China revenue before the AI ramp fully offsets it, FY2027 revenue lands near my p10 (~$36.6B) and the EPS compounding story breaks.

validated.preview_note: AMAT reports fiscal Q3 after the close Thursday. Setup: guidance is $8.95B ± $500M revenue and $3.36 ± $0.20 non-GAAP EPS, set in May when management raised its CY2026 equipment growth view to >30%. Three factors decide the print and the reaction. First, revenue magnitude versus the top of the range: record bookings, a deliberately enlarged build plan, and H2 CY2026 ramps at TSMC, Samsung and the DRAM makers argue for ~$9.1B; anything below $8.8B would suggest pushouts. Second, gross margin: Q2 printed 50.0% non-GAAP; confirmation of ~51% on richer DRAM/foundry mix matters more than the revenue beat itself. Third, cash: Q2's FCF collapsed to $210M on a $1.75B working-capital swing (inventory build, CP/tax timing) — investors need CFO back toward $2.5B and evidence the inventory converts. Watch also the strategic-investment marks that swung GAAP EPS +$0.80 last quarter (they reverse both ways) and China color ahead of tightening export rules. The reaction hinges on the Q4 guide: a midpoint ≥ $9.7B extends the AI-ramp narrative; a guide below ~$9.2B reframes H1 strength as pull-forward and the stock de-rates regardless of the beat.
validated.reasoning: Anchors are taken entirely from the filed record: Q2 FY2026 actuals and Q3 guidance from the May 14, 2026 8-K (0001628280-26-035071), Q1 FY2026 from the Feb 12, 2026 8-K (0001628280-26-007661), and FY2025 from the Nov 13, 2025 8-K (0001628280-25-051998). I deliberately deviate modestly above guidance midpoint on revenue ($9.10B vs $8.95B): management raised its CY2026 semi-equipment growth view to >30%, guided Q2 conservatively and beat by $260M, DRAM/HBM and foundry ramps are accelerating into H2 CY2026, and management pre-built inventory and logistics specifically for this window. Gross margin 50.8% GAAP (51.0% non-GAAP) extends the Q2 49.9%/50.0% trajectory on richer mix and volume leverage, partly offset by ramp and tariff costs. GAAP EPS ($3.46) sits far below non-GAAP ($3.52) relative to Q2's $0.65 gap because Q2's gap was a one-off unrealized gain on strategic investments; I assume marks are flat. CFO of $2.4B assumes the Q2 working-capital shock partially normalizes while inventory build continues; capex steps up to $700M/qtr on the EPIC Center and capacity. Buybacks step up to $1.8B given the depressed FCF in Q2 and the $10B authorization. The quarterly path then compounds the CY2026 ramp into FY2027 ($39.7B, +18%), decelerating to +7% in FY2028 and +3.5% in FY2029 as WFE cyclicality reasserts, with share count falling ~3%/yr. Balance sheet rolls strictly from the cash flow: cash 6,359 − 804 = 5,555; retained earnings 59,274 + 2,740 − 424 − 1,800 = 59,790; equity and liabilities derived so assets = liabilities + equity at every horizon.
